office_does: A Pend Oreille PUD commissioner sits on the three-member board that sets rates, budgets and policy for the county's public electric, water and broadband utility and hires its general manager, for a six-year term; every county voter elects each commissioner.
race_blurb: Open seat: Commissioner Curt Knapp is retiring. Newport teacher and former KUBS FM manager Gerry David Bradbury praises current management and puts the 2030 Boundary Dam power deal with Seattle City Light first. Retired technology executive Ernie Hood calls for fiscal discipline, more transparency on spending and care about rate pressure from state mandates and data centers.

candidates.summary: Lifelong Newport resident, Newport School District teacher and coach and longtime KUBS FM manager, once a PUD seasonal engineering assistant.
highlights: Calls the 2030 renegotiation of the Boundary Dam power agreement with Seattle City Light the top issue [S3]
Warns that unfunded state and federal environmental mandates could raise costs for ratepayers [S3]
Praises the current board's choice of general manager and management team [S3]
Former Newport city councilman; finished first in the district-only primary [S1][S4]

candidates.summary: Retired Navy electronics technician and technology-industry manager with an MBA, in the county about eight years, running on fiscal discipline and transparency.
highlights: Names aging infrastructure, data center growth and the Clean Energy Transformation Act as pressures on rates [S3]
Wants efficiency, caution about unnecessary spending and independent oversight [S3]
Asks for greater transparency in how major spending decisions are made [S3]
Wants the PUD to meet CETA's 2030 requirement while limiting the effect on ratepayers [S3]
